our_title: Single-vertex components still count as distance one in part pseudo-diameters
ran: cd /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G16-library-seq-api/repro; sh build.sh $INFRA/asan _p18; API-14/diam_p18 (and _p18_64): 4 of 7 cases now ok; 'path2 base0, {0,1} (diam 0,0) got: min=1 max=1 avg=1.000000 expected: min=0 ... FAIL', 'path2 base1 ... got: min=1 ... FAIL', 'path4 base0, {0,1,0,1} got: min=2 max=2 expected: min=1 FAIL'. Shipped data, SCOTCH_PTHREAD_NUMBER=1: gmap small1.grf m11x13.tgt -vm 'PartDiam min=1 max=1' (7.0.18) vs 'min=0 max=0' (patched); gpart 9 bump_b100000.grf now 'min=41 max=61 avg=47.333333' on 7.0.18 (base fixed). Patched (0001): all 7 ok, 32/64-bit; test_scotch_graph_map_view one-to-one case 'PartDiam min=0 max=0'.
severity_note: diagnostic output only, but every PartDiam ever printed is wrong by one and base-N graphs print zero; agrees with the review
evidence: 'distmax = 0; /* Start distances from zero */' then 'connval = distmax ++; /* Start from previous distance */': distmax is 1 before the BFS, so a component whose farthest vertex is at distance 0 returns 1.
upstream_change: a09f32492d Bugfix: compute connected components, distances and diameters properly [report R. Perry]

upstream_fix_review.details: Correct: vertnbr -> vertnnd bound (library_graph_map_view.c:129,133), first component now starts at distance 0, and the -1 return of graphMapView3 is now tested with memFree(domntab) and return (1) (lines 541-546), which is complete since domntab is the group leader. Wrong: 'connval = distmax ++' (line 136) post-increments distmax before the BFS, so distmax is a floor of connval + 1: a single-vertex component reports 1 instead of 0 (every part of a one-vertex-per-part mapping, small1/m11x13 prints 'PartDiam min=1 max=1'), and the chaining of disconnected components is inconsistent (component of diameter 0 adds 1, of diameter d>=1 adds d, with no gap between components). 32/64-bit identical.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Ours (7.0.17 0001) started distmax at -1 and kept 'connval = ++ distmax', giving 0 for singletons and chaining components as if joined by one edge; it also documented the return values of graphMapView3. His error-path check is equivalent to ours (he adds an errorPrint, slightly better). Ours is better on the arithmetic; the rebased 0001 keeps his error path and only changes the two distmax lines plus the header comment.

review_accuracy: accurate; its fix line (compare with vertnnd, start at 0, handle -1) is what the patch does. The review does not say what a disconnected part should report; the existing code chains components (sum of diameters plus one per extra component) and the patch keeps that, only removing the constant offset.
first_pass_critique: Right on status and evidence. Its preferred diff keeps counting from one and subtracts one at the return with a clamp ('(distmax > 0) ? (distmax - 1) : 0'), which hides the off-by-one rather than removing it and makes the error code collide with a legitimate value only by accident; it also bundled an unrelated API-22 hunk (graphPartOvlView return) into the same sketch. The preferred patch here starts distmax at -1 so that 'connval = ++ distmax' is zero for the first component, and checks the -1 return in the caller.

extra_instances.quote: connval = distmax ++;                         /* Start from previous distance */

fix_options.label: A. Start distmax at -1, pre-increment (rebased 0001)
fix_options.summary: distmax = -1; connval = ++ distmax: first component from 0, each next one from one past the previous diameter (components linked by an edge); doc of return values.
fix_options.tested: repro API-14 7/7 ok 32/64-bit; check_scotch_graph_map_view (new one-to-one case), check_scotch_graph_map, check_prog_gmap/gpart/gpart_remap/gpart_overlap 32/64-bit
fix_options.tradeoffs: Same numbers as our 7.0.17 patch. vs 7.0.18: single-vertex parts 1 -> 0; parts with k>1 components +1 per extra component where some component has diameter >= 1 (gpart 32 bump_imbal_32 -ro bump_old.map: 'min=16 max=40 avg=26.812500' -> 'min=16 max=41 avg=27.000000').
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Two-line change in his loop; keeps his error handling.

fix_options.label: B. Keep his chaining, drop the post-increment
fix_options.summary: connval = distmax: components chained without gap (sum of diameters); singletons 0.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Smallest diff; but a part made of isolated vertices reports 0, same as a single vertex, so disconnection becomes invisible.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches his comment 'Start from previous distance' literally.

ran: ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 mpirun --oversubscribe -np 1 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-playground/925301e5-494b-5a33-b598-8eaa63dd5c1d/scratchpad/work18/G16-library-seq-api/repro/API-18/dview_p18 m4x4_b1_ev.grf k4.tgt: sequential 'M CommDelta=0.657106', distributed 'M CommDelta=1.314211'; -np 3 bump.grf k9.tgt: sequential 'CommDelta=1.000000', distributed 'CommDelta=2.000000' (7.0.17 printed 1.000000 for unweighted graphs). upstream_change: 27f4193c38 Bugfix: compute distributed mapping delta from proper values [report R. Perry]

upstream_fix_review.details: He applied the review's formula verbatim, which our 7.0.17 audit had already flagged as off by a factor two: the distributed sums are edge-once (CommDilat at library_dgraph_map_view.c:135 divides by edgeglbnbr / 2) but edgeglbnbr counts arcs. Result: the weighted case moved from 0.406780 to 1.314211 (right value 0.657106), and the unweighted case, which was right in 7.0.17 (1.000000), is now 2.000000: a regression for every dgmap -v user (filed as PS3-G16-1). 32/64-bit identical.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 0007 used '(grafptr->edgeglbnbr / 2)', the same expression as the CommDilat line, and was verified line-for-line against SCOTCH_graphMapView. Ours is right; the rebased 0006 changes only that factor on top of his formula.

review_accuracy: diagnosis accurate; its formula '(cmexsum * edgeglbnbr) / (cmlosum * cmdisum)' is off by a factor two (dgraphMapStat returns edge-once sums, edgeglbnbr counts arcs): it would print 1.314212 here
first_pass_critique: Right, including the factor-two correction of the review. Its diff is a correct double-precision formula; the patch writes it with '(grafptr->edgeglbnbr / 2)' exactly as the CommDilat line ten lines above already does, so the three lines share one convention. The first pass did not build the gmap-vs-dgmap differential the user asked for.

upstream_fix_review.details: Halves the weighted arc sum after the average in SCOTCH_graphStat (library_graph.c:500) and SCOTCH_dgraphStat (library_dgraph_stat.c:250): this is the edge convention (our option A), consistent with the unweighted branches and the manual. Both twins done; average and variance unchanged; 32/64-bit verified. Not done: the manuals still say only 'the sum of all edge loads' (kept as doc commit 0004), the never-assigned DgraphStatData.edlosum (PS2-G16-2) remains, and library_dgraph_stat.c header date was not bumped (still 08 oct 2025, cosmetic).
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Same code as our 7.0.17 0004 hunk for hunk (ours also clarified the doc). Decision 'edge-load sum convention' is now settled by upstream: edge convention. PyScotch assertions that change (weighted graphs only, value halves): tests/pyscotch_base/test_interop.py:65 (14 -> 7), :181 (4 -> 2), :246 (4 -> 2), :314 (10 -> 5), :357 (8 -> 4); tests/pyscotch_base/test_graph.py:144 ((1,3,12) -> (1,3,6)); tests/hypothesis/test_graph_properties.py:356 (2 * sum(edge_weights) -> sum(edge_weights), and the comment above it). Unweighted ones (test_graph_advanced.py:59,71, hypothesis unit-weight branch) unchanged. Scotch's own printed output: gtst/dgtst 'Edge load ... sum=' halves for weighted graphs (m4x4_b1_ev 118 -> 59).

review_accuracy: accurate on the inconsistency; it leaves the convention open
first_pass_critique: Right on status and evidence; it preferred the arc convention on the strength of the internal Graph.edlosum field, i.e. the opposite of what the user manual and gtst's own 'Edge nbr' line support, and it did not touch the doc. Its alternative also mis-stated that edloavg would need a change (it does not: the average is the same over arcs and over edges). It also left the never-assigned DgraphStatData.edlosum field alone (PS2-G16-2).

fix_options.tradeoffs: none beyond the behaviour change already shipped
